name: CyberGhost VPN
tagline: Consumer VPN with thousands of servers in ~100 countries, apps for every platform, and a no-logs pitch.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: You can absolutely stand up your own VPN: WireGuard on a cheap VPS is a genuine one-sitting job and gives you an encrypted tunnel out of hostile coffee shop wifi. What you cannot build is the thing people actually buy, which is a fleet of servers in a hundred countries sharing one exit IP across thousands of strangers. Your personal VPN has an exit IP used by exactly one person, which means it is a worse privacy tool than the product and gets flagged by streaming services and fraud scores faster. Add the geo-hopping, the kill switches on iOS and Android and smart TVs, and the audited no-logs posture, and the gap is infrastructure, not code. Build the WireGuard box for the wifi threat model, keep paying someone else if the goal is location roulette or crowd anonymity.
coreLoopDIY: A WireGuard server on your own VPS with a script that mints client configs and QR codes for your phone.
requirements: A VPS you control, in a jurisdiction you have thought about
Root SSH access and a willingness to touch firewall rules
WireGuard clients on each device you want tunneled
whatYouLose: Exit IPs in dozens of countries; you get one, wherever your VPS lives
Crowd cover: a shared VPN IP hides you among thousands of users, yours points at you
Streaming unblocking, which is a permanent cat and mouse game you will lose
Polished native apps with kill switches, always-on profiles, and TV/router support
Third-party audits and a company whose business model depends on not logging you
moatNotes: A VPN is a logistics company that sells IP addresses. The software is the cheap part.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the product being sold is not encryption, it is other people. A commercial VPN's value comes from thousands of users leaving through the same handful of addresses in the same handful of countries, plus a support team fighting the endless war against streaming geoblocks and datacenter IP reputation lists. A personal WireGuard box gives you a clean tunnel off untrusted wifi and a stable home-ish IP, which is a real and useful thing, but it is a spotlight rather than a crowd. Add per-platform apps, always-on kill switches, and the trust theater of published audits, and the subscription keeps making sense for anyone whose threat model is not just the airport lounge.
notes: The tunnel is a one-sitting build; the hundred-country server fleet is not. The moat is scale infrastructure plus the anonymity that only comes from sharing an exit IP with strangers.
prompt:
Build me a self-hosted WireGuard VPN setup for personal use on a single Linux VPS.

Stack, no alternatives: Debian 12 on the server, WireGuard kernel module, bash scripts, nftables for firewalling. No Docker, no web UI, no accounts, no telemetry.

Deliver these files in this folder:
1. install.sh: idempotent server bootstrap. Installs wireguard-tools and qrencode, enables IPv4 and IPv6 forwarding via sysctl, generates the server keypair into /etc/wireguard with 0600 perms, writes wg0.conf listening on a UDP port read from .env, sets up nftables masquerade on the primary interface, enables wg-quick@wg0 with systemd.
2. add-client.sh NAME: generates a client keypair and preshared key, assigns the next free IP from the configured subnet, appends a [Peer] block to wg0.conf, hot-adds the peer with wg set so no reconnect is needed, writes clients/NAME.conf, and prints a terminal QR code for phone import.
3. remove-client.sh NAME: reverses all of the above, including the live wg set peer remove.
4. list-clients.sh: prints name, IP, last handshake, transfer totals in a readable table.
5. .env.example with WG_PORT, WG_SUBNET_V4, WG_SUBNET_V6, SERVER_PUBLIC_HOST, DNS_SERVERS. Real .env is gitignored.
6. README.md: exact commands in order, how to open the UDP port at the cloud provider firewall, and how to verify the tunnel with a curl to an IP echo service.

Default client configs to AllowedIPs 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 with PersistentKeepalive 25, but include a commented split-tunnel variant.

Explicitly out of scope: multi-region servers, load balancing, obfuscation or anti-DPI, a GUI, log rotation policy theater, and any claim that this makes you anonymous. Put a short honest paragraph in the README saying this hides traffic from the local network and your ISP, and nothing more, because the exit IP is yours alone.

Every script must fail loudly with set -euo pipefail and refuse to run as non-root.
